overview: A busy day on bpf-next dominated by two large series: Yonghong Song's 20-patch v3 series adding exception cleanup landing pads to bpf_throw() unwind support, and Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi's 11-patch v5 series fixing __uninit kfunc output buffer handling in the verifier. Several hash-map optimizations and a new set of TCP AutoLOWAT hooks for bpf_tcp_ops also landed.

patches.title: bpf: Accept the compiler's exception cleanup table at program load
patches.author: Yonghong Song
patches.summary: First patch of a 20-patch v3 series implementing exception cleanup landing pads for bpf_throw(). The series teaches the BPF loader to accept a compiler-generated .bpf_cleanup section, adds a new bpf_unwind_resume() kfunc, wires the landing pads into the verifier's CFG walk, and adds JIT support on both x86 and arm64. This enables BPF programs compiled with C++ exception semantics to run proper destructors when bpf_throw() unwinds the stack, closing a longstanding gap in BPF exception handling.

patches.title: bpf: Fix generic __uninit kfunc output buffers
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: Core fix in an 11-patch v5 series addressing incorrect verifier handling of kfunc arguments annotated __uninit. The patch corrects the verifier to treat such output buffers as write-only during argument checking, fixing a bug where uninitialized stack slots could be presented as readable memory. The series also adds support for multiple __uninit output arguments per kfunc call and ensures stack initialization is preserved for generic output buffers.

patches.title: bpf: tcp: Introduce bpf_tcp_ops.{enqueue,dequeue}_rcvq()
patches.author: Kuniyuki Iwashima
patches.summary: Second patch of a 7-patch series adding bpf_tcp_ops hooks for TCP AutoLOWAT, which allows BPF programs to dynamically adjust sk->sk_rcvlowat based on receive queue depth. The series introduces enqueue/dequeue callbacks for the receive queue, adds a new kfunc to adjust the lowat threshold, and wires up BPF_SOCK_OPS callback flags. This enables userspace-transparent receive buffering policies without kernel modifications.

patches.title: bpf: htab: Split htab_elem_lru and htab_elem_pcpu off of htab_elem
patches.author: T.J. Mercier
patches.summary: First patch of a 2-patch v5 series reducing memory consumption of BPF hash maps. By splitting the rarely-used LRU and per-CPU variants into separate structs, the series enables the second patch to shave 8 bytes off elem_size for hash maps with small keys, yielding meaningful memory savings at scale. This is the fifth iteration of a performance-focused series targeting large deployments with many map entries.

patches.title: bpf: Destroy callee-local dynptrs on subprog return
patches.author: Xu Yunxiang
patches.summary: Part of a 2-patch v5 series fixing verifier lifetime tracking for dynptrs local to a called subprogram. Previously, a dynptr created inside a subprog and not explicitly released would silently escape its scope; this patch teaches the verifier to synthesize teardown on subprog return. A companion patch in the same series fixes BTF pointer lifetime tracking for iterators.

patches.title: bpftool: Read ring buffer maps with event_pipe
patches.author: Tianyi Chen
patches.summary: First patch of a 2-patch v5 series adding event_pipe support to bpftool's ring buffer consumer. The patch lets bpftool read from a BPF ring buffer map and feed events into a named pipe, enabling integration with external log consumers without writing a dedicated BPF userspace program. This is the fifth revision, addressing review feedback on error handling and pipe lifecycle management.

patches.title: bpf: Speed up htab hashing for u32/u64 keys
patches.author: Mykyta Yatsenko
patches.summary: Optimizes the BPF hash table lookup path for the common case of 32-bit and 64-bit integer keys by bypassing the generic jhash path in favor of a faster direct multiplication hash. At Meta, hash maps with u32/u64 keys are extremely common, and this specialization reduces lookup latency measurably on hot paths. This is the initial v1 posting of the patch.
